subject: Renewal negotiation: rebalance committed run‑hours + burst safeguard
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@bluenova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T09:14:00Z
Subject: Renewal kickoff + capacity rebalance

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our conversation, I attached an updated renewal worksheet (bluenova-renewal-sheet-v2.xlsx) that shows two paths:

- Path A: modest uplift to committed run-hours (10% increase) with standard committed rate.
- Path B: smaller commit (+3%) plus a capped burst pool priced at a marginal blended rate for unpredictable traffic.

You mentioned internal pressure to keep headline pricing flat for the next 12 months while still getting predictable capacity for Q4. If you can share the internal procurement timeline I’ll align our commercial team and try to hold pricing during your evaluation window.

Next step: can you confirm which path you prefer and whether a temporary price-hold through 06/2029 (12 months) would be required to secure signoff? If procurement wants a purchase order instead of DocuSign, we can accept that but will need a PO by end of month to lock the rates.

Thanks —
Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bluenova-renewal-sheet-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@bluenova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff + capacity rebalance

Monica —

Appreciate the summary and the two paths. Quick answers: procurement wants a price hold for at least 12 months; they are open to a blended approach but will push back on any large uplift to committed run-hours. Q4 is the priority window — we need burst headroom without being penalised if traffic stays low.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Can you cap monthly surge spend at a predictable band for the 12‑month hold?
2) If we hit sustained high utilization for 3 months, can we trigger a softer true‑up rather than an automatic top‑up?

We can get a PO in July but procurement needs legal and pricing to be stable while they route it.

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Product Infrastructure
BlueNova Labs
ben.harper@bluenova.com

Attachment: none

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T08:37:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Renewal kickoff + capacity rebalance — strategic ask from BlueNova

Looping you both in — Ben wants: 12-month price hold, capped monthly surge band, and a softer true-up trigger after sustained high utilization. Procurement will need a ratified commercial to start the PO routing in early July.

Notes: BlueNova is a mid-size device telemetry customer (annualized run-hours ~ 1.2M token-hours). They’re greenfield for our Dedicated offering but currently on hosted. They prefer lower headline increases; they value predictable monthly spend.

Can we put together a proposed structure that preserves margin while providing the burst cap and a conditional true-up window? I also included the renewal worksheet they received. I’d like a quick executive-friendly one-pager we can send back to them.

—Monica

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T14:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal kickoff + capacity rebalance — proposed commercial

Monica / Laura —

Draft proposal (high level) to address BlueNova's asks while protecting our economics: 

1) Commit + burst split
   - Offer: 6% increase to committed run-hours (lower than their initial 10% ask) to keep headline uptick modest.
   - Complement with an explicit monthly burst pool ("Burst Band") equal to 20% of committed hours at a predictable incremental rate. Burst Band priced at an incremental blended rate 35% above committed rate (capped).

2) 12‑month conditional price hold
   - Hold committed rate for 12 months from effective date. If they exceed burst band for 3 consecutive months and sustained utilization is >85%, trigger a 30‑day negotiation window for a mid‑term true‑up. Not an automatic charge — requires mutual confirmation.

3) Surge cap and PO flow
   - Implement a soft monthly cap: if monthly burst spend would exceed X (we can set X as $50k for now based on worksheet), we send an alert and pause auto-billing of additional burst until a signed addendum or approved charge. If they prefer, we can accept a good‑faith PO to authorize surges up to that cap.

4) Approvals / concessions
   - Standard SLA and 99.9% availability on hosted product. Any SLA exceptions require Director sign‑off.
   - We can offer a one‑time onboarding credit of $10k (applied to first invoice) in exchange for a 12‑month term commitment and PO by 31‑Jul‑2028.

If you want to present this externally I’ll draft a one‑pager commercial and a redlined term sheet for legal. We should confirm the exact $ cap on surge with finance (I used $50k as placeholder).

Vivek
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposed-commercial-20280615.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@bluenova.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@bluenova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Proposal: Commit uplift + burst band + 12‑month price hold (BlueNova)

Hi Ben / Procurement —

Thanks for the clarity; attached is our proposed commercial reflecting the items we discussed:

- Commit increase: +6% to existing committed run-hours
- Burst Band: 20% of committed hours per month at incremental blended rate (capped)
- 12‑month conditional price hold on committed rate (effective on signature)
- Softer true‑up: triggered after 3 consecutive months >85% utilization; initiates 30‑day negotiation window (no automatic top‑up)
- Soft surge cap: alerts at projected $50k/month; additional surges require PO or signed addendum
- One‑time onboarding credit: $10,000 if PO is received by 2028‑07‑31

DocuSign packet: https://www.docusign.com/packet/0a7b9d-renewal-2028
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/BLU-7782

Please review and let me know if we can get procurement to route a PO or if you prefer to sign via DocuSign. If procurement needs a faster legal turnaround we can prioritize the redlines.

Best,
Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@bluenova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@bluenova.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal: Commit uplift + burst band + 12‑month price hold (BlueNova)

Monica —

This looks good and addresses our priorities. Procurement will start routing a PO for the 12‑month hold and the +6% commit. Two small clarifications they asked: 

1) Can the burst cap be expressed as an absolute dollar value on the contract (you suggested $50k) rather than a percent? Procurement prefers an absolute cap to trigger approvals.
2) SLA question: procurement asked whether the 99.9% uptime applies to our hosted region with cross‑region failover included (they prefer cross‑region fallback documented).

If you can update the packet to show a $50k/month soft cap and a short SLA note on the cross‑region behavior we’ll approve and route the PO. We intend to return a signed PO by 07/10.

Ben
VP, Product Infrastructure, BlueNova Labs
ben.harper@bluenova.com
